lmsArticle.title: 📦 Snap & Roll: Raft Log Compaction in Serverless Functions
lmsArticle.subtitle: Keep your serverless Raft cluster lean by snapshotting logs to durable storage.
lmsArticle.excerpt: Keep your serverless Raft cluster lean by snapshotting logs to durable storage.
lmsArticle.content:
> **TLDR:** In serverless Raft, the log can balloon fast because functions are stateless. Persisting compacted snapshots to object storage lets you restart a node in seconds and keep state machine size manageable.  

### ⚠️ The Gotcha  
Serverless functions (e.g., AWS Lambda, Azure Functions) terminate after a short run. A Raft node that stores its log in memory loses it on shutdown. If you restart the function, you must replay the entire log from the last snapshot. With a growing log, this replay can take minutes or even hours, breaking the low‑latency guarantees of a serverless state machine.  

### 🛠️ The Solution & Trade‑offs  
1. **Persist Snapshots** – After every *N* log entries or at a regular interval, serialize the state machine’s current state and the last committed index. Store this blob in durable object storage (S3, Blob, etc.).  
2. **Store Metadata** – Keep a small metadata file that records the snapshot’s index, term, and a checksum. This allows a new function instance to validate the snapshot before loading.  
3. **Incremental Snapshots** – Rather than full snapshots each time, store diffs (e.g., using a Merkle tree or diff‑patch). This reduces bandwidth and storage costs.  
4. **Lazy Loading** – On function start, load the latest snapshot into memory, then replay only the entries that follow the snapshot’s index. Because the snapshot contains the state machine’s entire state, the replay window is tiny.  
5. **Cold‑start Optimisation** – Cache the snapshot in a shared in‑memory store (e.g., Redis, DynamoDB DAX) for the next few invocations to avoid hitting object storage each time.  

**Trade‑offs**:  
- **Latency vs. Cost** – Full snapshots give the fastest restarts but cost more storage; incremental snapshots save space but add computation during snapshot creation.  
- **Consistency** – You must ensure the snapshot is written atomically; otherwise, a corrupt snapshot can bring the node down.  

### 🔁 Architecture Kit Diagram  
```architecture
{
  "version": 1,
  "title": "Serverless Raft Snapshot Flow",
  "description": "How a stateless function loads a Raft snapshot from object storage",
  "view": "data-flow",
  "pattern": "reactive-pull",
  "direction": "LR",
  "groups": [
    { "id": "function", "label": "Raft Function", "tone": "slate" },
    { "id": "storage", "label": "Object Storage", "tone": "neutral" },
    { "id": "cache", "label": "Shared Cache", "tone": "neutral" }
  ],
  "nodes": [
    { "id": "func_start", "component": "function", "label": "Function Init", "group": "function" },
    { "id": "cache_lookup", "component": "cache", "label": "Check Cache", "group": "cache" },
    { "id": "storage_fetch", "component": "storage", "label": "Fetch Snapshot", "group": "storage" },
    { "id": "load_snapshot", "component": "function", "label": "Deserialize Snapshot", "group": "function" },
    { "id": "replay_logs", "component": "function", "label": "Replay Log Entries", "group": "function" }
  ],
  "edges": [
    { "from": "func_start", "to": "cache_lookup", "kind": "request" },
    { "from": "cache_lookup", "to": "load_snapshot", "kind": "cache hit" },
    { "from": "cache_lookup", "to": "storage_fetch", "kind": "miss" },
    { "from": "storage_fetch", "to": "load_snapshot", "kind": "data" },
    { "from": "load_snapshot", "to": "replay_logs", "kind": "data" }
  ],
  "takeaway": { "title": "Takeaway", "body": "Persist compacted snapshots to durable storage and load them lazily to keep serverless Raft fast and small." }
}
```

### 📈 When to Use  
- **High‑frequency writes** where the log can outgrow memory in a few minutes.  
- **Cost‑sensitive environments** where you want to keep the function runtime short.  
- **Regulatory compliance** requiring state to be recoverable after a crash or function termination.  

By treating snapshots as first‑class citizens in your serverless Raft design, you keep state machine size under control and ensure that cold starts remain a brief, predictable event rather than a cascading delay.

seriesList.name: Architecture Patterns for Production Systems
seriesList.description: High-level design is only half the battle; the other half is surviving production. This series explores the architectural patterns required to build resilient, scalable, and maintainable systems. We dive into the trade-offs of microservices vs. monoliths, event-driven architectures, caching strategies, and data consistency models. Each post focuses on proven patterns that solve common bottlenecks in high-traffic production environments, helping you move from "it works on my machine" to "it works at scale."

seriesList.name: Data Structures and Algorithms
seriesList.description: Master the core of computer science. This series demystifies Data Structures and Algorithms, from Big O to graph theory. Learn to write efficient, scalable code and ace your technical interviews with confidence.

seriesList.name: How It Works: Internals Explained
seriesList.description: Ever wondered what actually happens when you trigger a function, commit a transaction, or deploy a container? This series peels back the layers of abstraction to explore the low-level mechanics of modern technology. From database engines and operating system internals to the hidden plumbing of distributed systems, we dive deep into the source code and architectural designs that make complex software work. No magic, just engineering.

seriesList.name: Low-Level Design Guide
seriesList.description: Good architecture is built on a foundation of solid low-level design. This series is a deep dive into the "micro" side of software engineering—focusing on class design, object-oriented principles (SOLID), and tactical design patterns. We explore how to translate requirements into clean, maintainable code, handle concurrency at the component level, and define clear interfaces. Whether you're preparing for LLD interviews or looking to sharpen your day-to-day coding craftsmanship, this guide provides the blueprints for building modular software.

seriesList.name: Machine Learning Fundamentals
seriesList.description: This series breaks down complex mathematical theories and algorithms into simple, intuitive explanations with practical examples, making AI accessible to everyone from beginners to aspiring data scientists.

seriesList.name: Software Engineering Principles
seriesList.description: Writing code is easy; engineering software that lasts is hard. This series explores the core philosophies and mental models that define professional software development. We go beyond syntax to discuss the timeless principles of modularity, abstraction, testing strategies, and technical debt management. Whether we’re discussing the Zen of Python or the rigors of formal verification, this series provides a high-level perspective on how to think like an engineer, not just a coder.
